prompt.content:
You are a text compressor. Your task is to compress the given passage into the shortest possible form while preserving the key information. The compressed text will be read by another AI that must answer questions about the original passage using ONLY your compression.

You will NOT see the questions. You must preserve all important facts, relationships, names, numbers, dates, and causal chains.

Output format:
<reasoning>What information is essential to preserve and why</reasoning>
<compressed>Your compressed version here</compressed>

Compress the following passage:

The PageRank algorithm, developed by Larry Page and Sergey Brin at Stanford in 1996, forms the foundation of Google's search ranking system. It models the web as a directed graph where each page's importance is determined by the number and quality of links pointing to it. The algorithm uses a damping factor of 0.85, representing the probability that a random web surfer continues clicking links rather than jumping to a random page. PageRank is computed iteratively until convergence, typically requiring 50-100 iterations. The sum of all PageRank values across the web equals 1.

Compress the following passage:

Lithium-ion batteries work by shuttling lithium ions between a cathode (typically lithium cobalt oxide) and an anode (typically graphite) through an electrolyte. During discharge, lithium ions flow from anode to cathode, generating electric current. During charging, the process reverses. These batteries have an energy density of 150-260 Wh/kg, roughly three times that of lead-acid batteries. They typically retain 80% capacity after 500-1,000 charge cycles. Thermal runaway, where the battery overheats uncontrollably, is the primary safety concern, occurring above 150 degrees Celsius.
